hints.title: Complementary Counting
hints.text: Counting numbers with repeated digits directly is intricate. Instead, count how many numbers have no repeated digits at all, and subtract that quantity from n.

hints.title: Shorter Length Permutations
hints.text: For numbers with strictly fewer digits than n, compute counts via permutations: the leading digit has 9 choices (1-9), and each following position chooses from the remaining unused digits.

hints.title: Prefix Matching and Tight Bound
hints.text: Iterate through digits of n from left to right. For each position, try placing all strictly smaller unused digits and multiply by permutations of remaining positions. Stop when a duplicate digit is encountered in n.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Iterating through all integers from 1 to N checking for duplicate digits takes O(N log N) which exceeds the time limit for N = 10^9.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Counting unique-digit numbers combinatorially runs in O(log N) time with minimal auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should convert the problem to counting unique digit numbers using combinatorics or digit DP.
complexity.notes: Permutations formula P(m, c) computes arrangements of c items from m candidates.
